direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels very different from his traditional style, as it is more for a grand scale and less artsy; His direction on a macroscale has punk influence that makes this feel like a polished Guy Ritchie movie; The direction on a microscale is still pretty traditional to his style, as it is still a movie driven by a protagonist who has to go through the story while processing past traumas; The direction on a microscale is still less serious than his other movies, as it is more light-hearted fun; The storytelling is both similar to his style, as it follows a multifaceted protagonist who goes through personal struggles to get through the story, but different in the fact that it is less serious and feels more like a polished Guy Ritchie movie; They build tension pretty well, as they give the protagonist enough personality and backstory that you care about them and the hardships they go through, even though the story can be a little surface level at times

performance.comments: Plays the main character of an Aronofsky movie well, as he captures the character's internal struggles and complexities, but is also so infectiously charismatic that he makes this movie very entertaining; He has really good chemistry with Smith and Kravitz
Kind of just plays a character with no personality, but is carried by someone who is an experienced actress
Really enjoyed her performance as her charisma and screen presence was really entertaining, and it also helped that her chemistry with Butler was really good
Really liked his British Punk persona, as it really, really nudged this movie in the 'Guy Ritchie' direction; He has good chemistry with Butler
Kind of just a stoic Hebrew character, but his dynamic with D'Onofrio is interesting
Kind of just a stoic Hebrew character, but his dynamic with Schreiber is interesting

cast.comments: Everyone just plays these entertaining characters that make this movie feel punky and more like a "Guy Ritchie" movie

story.comments: The concept is pretty interesting as it is a punky crime thriller movie you would see from a director like 'Guy Ritchie' on the surface, but at its core, it is a typical Aronofsky movie that follows a singular protagonist who goes through the story, progressing through their past traumas; the plot structure is pretty simple and surface level; character writing is good for the protagonist as it provides some depth into their storyline of being a failed baseball player and how their past trauma makes them a scared and vulnerable person, but the remaining characters are more caricatures you would see in an entertaining 'Guy Ritchie' punky crime thriller movie

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is entertaining, with its profound moments; the humor is surprisingly present for an Aronofsky film as it makes the movie feel entertaining; the symbolism is present in how it follows the traumas of the protagonist, but is definitely a lot less deep than his other character studies; the foreshadowing is expected for the bookends, but the movie takes you on different turns that you definitely don't expect

score.comments: Really liked the punk-inspired themes, as it helped add to the tone of the movie

soundtrack.comments: Really liked the punk inspired themes as it helped add to the tone of the movie

cinematography.comments: Feels pretty high-budget and not something you would see from an Aronofsky movie as it makes this movie an entertaining action movie at times, the way the movie moves throughout New York; Not a huge fan of the high shutter speed shots in the action sequences

editing.comments: Make this movie feel like a polished Guy Ritchie movie; helped elevate the overall production value and make the movie feel like an entertaining crime thriller

sound.comments: Helped give the movie its pop and give it a punk feel

visual_effects.comments: Mostly practical effects, and they did a pretty good job of using them

production_design.comments: 1998 New York is very integral to the story as it felt like another character in this movie, the way they navigate the city

makeup.comments: Helps show the beating the characters took throughout the movie

review.pacing: Pacing is definitely on the fast side as this movie constantly moves, even though the movie feels like it runs in circles at moments
review.climax: Climax kinda feels like it stretched itself, but it is still entertaining; the ending feels like the right ending
review.tone: Tone is heavily inspired by punk culture, as the movie feels like a polished 'Guy Ritchie' movie
review.final_notes: Really enjoyed how they did the credits as it made me want to stay and watch
review.overall: Overall, a good movie that is a fun and entertaining punky crime thriller that feels like a polished 'Guy Ritchie' movie;  the movie on the surface feels nothing like a typical Aronofsky film as it plays off as a high-budget, entertaining comedy, but at its core, it is very Aronofsky as it is still a character study into a protagonist going through past traumas that still haunt them, and this comes to life through Austin Butler's charismatic performance
